name: Typographic Explainer Intro Collage
use_when: A documentary explainer needs a concise title/opening graphic made from words, labels, arrows, icons, and simple shapes.
The intro should establish an editorial style before maps, charts, or documents begin.
The project has cleared logos/icons or generic substitutes that can be arranged safely.
avoid_when: The intro would copy another publisher's logo, protected mark, or exact trade dress.
The viewer needs immediate evidence or footage more than a designed title sequence.
The typography stack would duplicate captions or make the premise harder to read.

timeline_pattern.pattern: background -> primary_title_word -> secondary_label -> circle_or_marker -> arrow -> source_or_tool_label -> staggered_in_animations -> compound_clip -> trim_to_finished_intro
timeline_pattern.hierarchy_rule: One word or phrase should dominate; labels and icons support it.
timeline_pattern.order_rule: Stagger entrances in the order the viewer should read the idea.
timeline_pattern.compound_rule: Build the intro longer than needed, group it, then trim the compound to the actual completed animation.
timeline_pattern.family_rule: Use a project-specific font family lane: editorial serif for documentary gravity, clean sans for utility labels, and display type only for the dominant title word.
timeline_pattern.brand_intro_rule: If the intro is for a creator/show brand rather than a documentary title, include brand identity, proof or authority, and outcome instead of only decorative title texture.

motion.rule: Use simple wipe, fade, showing-up, and short slide animations; keep typography readable through the entrance.

keyframe_values.build_length: Create intro elements at around 8-10 seconds when timing is uncertain, then trim the compound to the finished 3-6 second range.
keyframe_values.arrow_wipe: Use a directional wipe that travels from source label to destination label.
keyframe_values.label_rotation: Small rotations can create handmade editorial texture when they do not hurt readability.
keyframe_values.fade_out: Use a short fade out from the completed compound into the next scene.

sound.rule: Use small pops, ticks, or whooshes only on meaningful text/icon entrances; the intro must not bury narration.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions during the intro when the designed text already carries the same words.

color.rule: Use a restrained editorial palette with enough contrast between text, marker shapes, and paper background. Accent colors should identify meaning or category, not random decoration.

implementation.ffmpeg: Layer drawtext, image overlays, masks, fades, and wipe animations; pre-render the intro as a reusable segment after readability checks.
implementation.remotion: Create a TypographicIntro component with ordered elements, entrance type, palette, arrow direction, and compound duration metadata.
implementation.blender: Use text objects, planes, and curves for title/arrow layout when a rendered 3D or camera scene is needed.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use text layers, shape/image masks, wipe/fade/showing-up animations, optional rotations, W trims, and a compound clip for the finished intro.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text/shapes, imported icons, Linear Wipe or opacity keyframes, then nest the intro sequence for timing and transition control.

common_mistakes: Copying a publisher logo or exact title identity without rights.
Animating too many words with equal emphasis.
Leaving the intro at the build length after the animation finishes.
Letting captions duplicate the designed title text.
Using arrows or labels whose reading order is unclear.
Mixing font families without a documentary, label, or headline role.
Building a beautiful intro collage that never tells the viewer why to trust the creator or what outcome to expect.
qc: Can the viewer read the title/idea in the intended order?
Does one word or phrase clearly dominate the hierarchy?
Are all logos/icons cleared, generic, or project-owned?
Is the compound intro trimmed to the finished animation rather than padded dead time?
Does the fade or transition into the next scene feel intentional?
Do font families and accent colors have clear roles?
If this is a branded intro, does it communicate brand, proof, and outcome before the body starts?
